title: Host the native YEIS galaxy renderer and picking inside the existing React Three Fiber canvas

scope.subject: Galaxy renderer and cross-scale camera migration

research_summary: The model/data migration is complete, but the current YEIS mode still renders the local V2 GalaxyScene, so the product does not yet reuse YEIS's strongest cross-scale rendering assets. A compatibility PoC against the pinned MIT snapshot proved that StarPoints, ProcStarPoints, GalaxyCloud, GalaxySprites, CameraController and Input can run directly inside the existing R3F 8 / Three 0.185.1 Canvas with logarithmicDepthBuffer: no iframe, second canvas, or upstream app shell is required. The 109,401-star HYG catalog, procedural tiers, galaxy cloud/sprites, floating-origin camera state and native pick methods can therefore be reused nearly verbatim. Native catalog picks must resolve through the existing HIP crosswalk before falling back to YEIS generation, and Hero remains an explicit overlay. Choose a narrow R3F host around the pinned upstream renderer classes; add only React lifecycle disposal hooks where the upstream whole-app ownership model otherwise leaks listeners/GPU resources.

sources.finding: The pinned MIT snapshot contains the native star point clouds, procedural stars, galaxy cloud/sprites, floating-origin camera controller, input and shaders already proven with the selected universe model.
React Three Fiber exposes the existing Three scene, renderer, camera and frame loop through hooks, allowing foreign Three objects/classes to be hosted without a second canvas.
Three WebGLRenderer supports logarithmicDepthBuffer at renderer creation, matching the cross-scale depth strategy used by the native YEIS path.

search_ladder.conclusion: The full YEIS app contains the renderer, but importing its product shell would duplicate routing/UI/runtime; reuse the renderer closure only.
The existing R3F Canvas can host the native YEIS Three objects and frame loop directly; this avoids a second renderer/application.
Reuse StarPoints, ProcStarPoints, GalaxyCloud, GalaxySprites, CameraController and Input as the renderer/camera subsystem, keeping upstream algorithms intact.
Reuse native pick methods and shader files rather than porting/recreating star picking, magnitude/color logic or galaxy shaders.

coverage_matrix.capability: real 109,401-star field and native magnitude/color rendering
procedural stars and near/far galaxy scale regimes

coverage_matrix.decision: Do not embed/fork the upstream application.

coverage_matrix.capability: native star picking with observed NASA override
coverage_matrix.decision: Reuse upstream pick() and resolve star ids through the HIP-aware bridge.
Add narrow dispose hooks only; do not rewrite renderer algorithms.

candidates.reason: Provides maximum renderer coverage but introduces a duplicate product runtime/UI/canvas and weakens shared state integration.

candidates.source: local rewrite based on upstream reference

candidates.name: Reuse YEIS StarPoints/ProcStarPoints native pick methods
candidates.reason: Preserves upstream screen-space picking behavior and lets physical stars route through the existing HIP override without rebuilding hit testing.

decision.rationale: Use the exact pinned YEIS renderer/camera/picking subsystems as guests of the existing R3F Canvas. This maximizes mature reuse and cross-scale fidelity without importing the upstream application or creating a second WebGL runtime.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: The full app covers more immediately but duplicates the website runtime and product UI; the R3F-hosted native closure retains the valuable renderer with much less coupling.
Keeping V2 is cheaper locally but preserves the duplicate galaxy implementation the mother-engine migration is intended to retire.

decision.fallback: If one native renderer class cannot be hosted safely in R3F, retain the surrounding native stack and substitute only that class with the existing local renderer; do not abandon the full native path for a small local incompatibility.
